title: Burisma board fees paid into Rosemont Seneca Bohai (Hunter Biden and Devon Archer)
description: Per the House Oversight majority's third bank-records memo, Burisma Holdings put Hunter Biden and Devon Archer on its board in spring 2014 at an agreed rate the memo describes as '$1 Million Each per Year' and paid $83,333.33 per month each into Rosemont Seneca Bohai, the firm Hunter co-owned with Archer, totaling $3,321,379.49 from 2014 to 2015.
people: Hunter Biden (Burisma board member; co-owner of Rosemont Seneca Bohai); Devon Archer (Burisma board member; co-owner of Rosemont Seneca Bohai); Mykola Zlochevsky (Burisma owner (payer)); Vadym Pozharsky (Burisma corporate secretary who acted for Zlochevsky)
investigation_status: Examined by House Oversight (2023-24) and cited in the Aug. 2024 impeachment-inquiry report; no charges arising from the Burisma payments; Hunter Biden's Dec. 1, 2024 pardon covers conduct from Jan. 1, 2014.
dispute: Oversight Democrats' spokesperson (Aug. 9, 2023): 'none of the bank records he has released show any payments to Joe Biden'; Ranking Member Raskin said the records concern 'financial transactions that do not involve the president' (Fox News). The Democratic staff memo (Aug. 19, 2024) cites Burisma-linked witnesses Sally Painter and Karen Tramontano, who testified they knew of no financial arrangement involving Joe Biden and his son's Burisma work.
conflicting_figures: Fox News's summary of the memo gives one total ($3,321,379.49) for both men. It does not say explicitly whether that is combined or per person, though $83,333.33 x 2 x about 20 months matches a combined total. Hunter's own share is not stated.
curation_note: Total includes partner Devon Archer's share (not family). Before his presidency (vice presidency); counted in the 'before taking office' total.
validation_path: House Oversight majority bank-records memo of Aug. 9, 2023 (19 pages, redacted bank-statement screenshots), linked from the committee release and public. The underlying subpoenaed bank records are not fully public.

title: Popoviciu-linked Bladon Enterprises pays Robinson Walker LLC; about $1.04 million reaches Biden family accounts
description: House Oversight Republicans' May 10, 2023 memo says Bladon Enterprises, reported to be Romanian businessman Gabriel Popoviciu's Cypriot company, paid Rob Walker's Robinson Walker LLC over $3 million from November 2015 to May 2017, of which Biden family accounts received about $1.038 million. In an Aug. 7, 2024 court filing, special counsel prosecutors said Popoviciu hired Hunter Biden to try to get U.S. agencies to investigate the Romanian case against him, under an agreement described as real-estate 'management services.'
people: Gabriel Popoviciu (Payer (through Bladon Enterprises, per committee)); Hunter Biden (Hired by Popoviciu, per prosecutors; recipient via Owasco P.C. and RSTP II); Rob Walker (Owner of Robinson Walker LLC, the pass-through account); Hallie Biden (Listed recipient)
investigation_status: Prosecutors raised it as background in Hunter Biden's tax case (C.D. Cal. filing, Aug. 7, 2024). No charges relate to Popoviciu, and Hunter Biden was pardoned Dec. 1, 2024.
dispute: Hunter Biden's lawyers said he has been 'the target of politically motivated attacks and conspiracy theories' and 'has never been charged with any crime relating to these unfounded allegations' (AP). The Democratic staff memo (Aug. 2024) says Joe Biden had no involvement in Hunter's work for Popoviciu and the special counsel's filing does not implicate him. NPR noted a 2019 New York Times report found no evidence of improper actions by then-Vice President Biden. White House spokesman Ian Sams called Comer's claims 'baseless' (Washington Examiner).
conflicting_figures: Family share: about $1.038 million (memo, per Washington Examiner), 'over a million dollars' (committee release), 'more than $1 million' (NBC). Total into Robinson Walker: 'over $3 million' (memo). Prosecutors' filing says the business associate was paid 'more than $3 million' and split it with Hunter and another partner (AP). NBC described the payer as a company controlled by a 'Romanian official accused of corruption'; other outlets call Popoviciu a businessman.
curation_note: Documented transfer into a venture or account of a Biden family member; purpose disputed. Before his presidency (vice presidency 2014–16 or private citizen 2017–20), so counted in the 'before taking office' total. No record shows these funds reaching Joe Biden.
validation_path: House Oversight majority bank-records memo of May 10, 2023 (public PDF). Special counsel filing of Aug. 7, 2024 in U.S. v. Biden, C.D. Cal. No. 2:23-cr-00599-MCS, public on PACER.

title: Vice President Biden's push to oust Ukraine Prosecutor General Viktor Shokin (Burisma-related allegation disputed)
description: Ukraine's parliament removed Prosecutor General Viktor Shokin in March 2016 after Vice President Biden pressed for his dismissal. Republicans have alleged the push was tied to Burisma, which was paying Hunter Biden at the time (BF-01). Democrats and fact-checkers cite CNN reporting that the U.S. wanted Shokin out 'because he was soft on corruption,' a position shared by bipartisan U.S. policy and EU allies.
people: Joe Biden (Vice President; pressed for the dismissal); Viktor Shokin (Ukraine's prosecutor general, removed)
investigation_status: Examined in the House impeachment inquiry. The FBI informant claim of Burisma bribes was later charged as fabricated (BF-22). No official finding that the dismissal benefited Burisma.
dispute: Democratic fact sheet: Biden's push was consistent with bipartisan U.S. policy and EU allies, aimed at a prosecutor 'soft on corruption' (CNN), and a fact-check says the effort was for not cracking down enough on corruption, 'including at Burisma.' PolitiFact (cited there) says claims the committee implicated Biden in bribery overstate the evidence. The Democratic memo (Aug. 2024) says Biden led a 'bipartisan, international coalition' pressing Ukraine. The Republican report's own Shokin section could not be opened for this dataset.
validation_path: Contemporaneous reporting (NYT, Mar. 30, 2016) and Verkhovna Rada vote records (public). State Department and EU statements of 2015-16 were not opened for this dataset.
primary_source_title: House Oversight Committee Democrats — Fact v. Fiction: The Firing of Ukraine Prosecutor General Viktor Shokin

description: House Oversight Republicans' first bank-records memo shows State Energy HK Limited wired $3 million to Rob Walker's Robinson Walker LLC on March 1, 2017. The LLC then sent $1,065,692 in 16 payments between March 6 and May 18, 2017 to accounts labeled 'Biden,' Hallie Biden, Owasco P.C., JBBSR Inc, RSTP II LLC and First Clearing LLC.
people: Rob Walker (Owner of Robinson Walker LLC, recipient of the $3 million); Hunter Biden (Recipient via Owasco P.C., an entity the committee says he controlled); James Biden (The memo says companies associated with him were among recipients); Hallie Biden (Received $25,000 (Mar. 20, 2017) per the memo's table)

Rob Walker told the committee Biden 'was never involved in any of the business activities we pursued' (ABC News).
conflicting_figures: The memo's text says Hallie Biden received two payments totaling $35,000, but its table lists one $25,000 payment. The $1,065,692 total includes a $100,000 wire to First Clearing LLC that the committee says 'was intended for Hunter Biden or one of his companies' and was still investigating; amount_low excludes it. The memo also says family members received 'over $1.3 million' from Walker-related accounts in 2015-2017. NBC and NPR summaries of the GOP claims tie State Energy HK to CEFC; the March 2023 memo itself does not.

title: CEFC China Energy pays $4.8 million over 14 months to Hunter and James Biden entities (Hudson West III)
description: The Washington Post, reviewing bank statements and government and court records, reported that CEFC China Energy and its executives paid $4.8 million over 14 months to entities controlled by Hunter Biden and James Biden. The payments flowed under an Aug. 2, 2017 Hudson West III agreement that set a $500,000 retainer for Hunter plus monthly stipends of $100,000 (Hunter) and $65,000 (James), and about $1.4 million moved from Hunter's account to James Biden's Lion Hall Group.
people: Hunter Biden (Party to the Hudson West III agreement; account recipient); James Biden ($65,000 monthly stipend; Lion Hall Group received about $1.4 million); Ye Jianming (CEFC chairman); Gongwen Dong (CEFC executive who signed the Aug. 2, 2017 agreement)
investigation_status: Covered by the House Oversight inquiry and the Aug. 2024 impeachment report. Neither Hunter nor James Biden was charged over CEFC. Hudson West III was dissolved Nov. 2, 2018.
dispute: The Post 'did not find evidence that Joe Biden personally benefited from or knew details about the transactions with CEFC,' which came after he left the vice presidency and before his 2020 campaign. House Republicans say part of the money reached Joe Biden through a $40,000 check (BF-09); Democrats and FactCheck.org say that check repaid a documented loan.
conflicting_figures: Initial wire: $5 million into Hudson West III on Aug. 8, 2017 (Washington Post). The House GOP's Nov. 1, 2023 release attributes it to Northern International Capital, 'a Chinese company affiliated with CEFC.' The Post also reports 'at least $3.79 million' paid to Hunter-linked accounts through CEFC consulting contracts and does not reconcile that figure with the $4.8 million.
curation_note: Documented transfer into a venture or account of a Biden family member; purpose disputed. Before his presidency (vice presidency 2014–16 or private citizen 2017–20), so counted in the 'before taking office' total. No record shows these funds reaching Joe Biden.
validation_path: Washington Post article (Mar. 30, 2022) citing bank records released by Sen. Grassley, court documents and laptop files. The House Oversight majority release of Nov. 1, 2023 reproduces part of the money trail. Underlying records are partly public through Senate and House releases.
primary_source_title: The Washington Post (via Anchorage Daily News) — Inside Hunter Biden's multimillion-dollar deals with a Chinese energy company

title: $40,000 'loan repayment' check from James and Sara Biden to Joe Biden
description: Sara Biden wrote Joe Biden a $40,000 check dated Sept. 3, 2017, memo 'loan repayment.' House Republicans trace the funds to CEFC money: a $5 million wire on Aug. 8, 2017, $400,000 to Hunter's Owasco P.C., $150,000 from Hunter to Lion Hall Group on Aug. 14, and a $50,000 cash move to the couple's personal account on Aug. 28. Democrats and FactCheck.org point to records showing Joe Biden had wired $40,000 to the same joint account on July 28, 2017.
people: Joe Biden (Payee; private citizen at the time); James Biden (Joint account holder (payer)); Sara Biden (Signed the check)
investigation_status: Cited in the Aug. 2024 impeachment report. No charges, and James and Sara Biden were pardoned Jan. 19-20, 2025.
dispute: GOP (Comer, Nov. 1, 2023): '$40,000 in laundered China money ended up in Joe Biden's bank account.' Democrats' fact sheet: Joe Biden wired $40,000 from an attorney trust account on July 28, 2017 and the check repaid it 37 days later, into the same account. FactCheck.org found the records consistent with a short-term, no-interest loan but found no formal loan document. A committee spokesperson told the Washington Examiner the records do not clearly show the July wire came from Joe Biden's personal funds.
conflicting_figures: Character of the payment: 'laundered China money' (GOP) versus 'loan repayment' (memo line, Democrats). The amount, date and memo line are not disputed.
curation_note: Transfers to Joe Biden as a private citizen, labeled loan repayments or reimbursements; source and purpose disputed. Shown, not added.
validation_path: Check image and wire records reproduced in the House Oversight majority release (Nov. 1, 2023) and the Democrats' fact sheet (both public PDFs). The attorney trust account statements have not been released in full.

title: Americore Health lends James Biden $600,000 ($400,000 Jan. 12; $200,000 Mar. 1, 2018)

Per the Washington Examiner, the company later said it had improperly classified the payment as a loan.

White House spokesman Ian Sams said the committee had 'turned up zero evidence of wrongdoing by President Biden' (CBS News). The Democrats' fact sheet says this repayment went into a different Joe Biden account than the original wire came from.
conflicting_figures: Comer's letter says no records in the committee's possession show a large loan payment from Joe to James. The Democratic fact sheet reproduces a $200,000 wire from the attorney trust account on Jan. 12, 2018.

title: Joe and Jill Biden's post-vice-presidency income: $16.6 million AGI in 2017-2019 (books, speeches, Penn)
description: Tax returns released in 2019-2020 show Joe and Jill Biden's adjusted gross income was $11,031,309 (2017), $4,580,437 (2018) and $985,233 (2019), up from $396,456 in 2016. CNN reported $13.3 million of the 2017-18 total came from books and related speeches. PolitiFact cites Publishers Weekly's report of an $8 million three-book Flatiron deal and says the income was routed through two S corporations, CelticCapri Corp. and Giacoppa Corp.
people: Joe Biden (Earner (private citizen)); Jill Biden (Co-filer; about $700,000 in speaking fees)

dispute: PolitiFact rated 'Half True' a viral claim implying the income was unexplained, finding the returns and disclosures 'substantially explain' it. CNN: 30 paid book-tour speeches brought $1.8 million and 19 other engagements $2.4 million. Federal income tax paid was $3.7 million (2017) and $1.5 million (2018).

title: Hunter Biden's 10% BHR stake: 2021 divestment claim and transfer to lender Kevin Morris
description: Hunter Biden held a 10% stake in Shanghai-based Bohai Harvest RST (BHR), which he and partners founded in 2013, through his company Skaneateles. His attorney told the New York Times in 2021 that he no longer held any interest, and Kevin Morris testified in January 2024 that he took over the stake by acquiring Skaneateles in 2021 and had received no BHR payouts.
people: Hunter Biden (Former 10% holder via Skaneateles); Kevin Morris (Acquired Skaneateles and the BHR stake in 2021)

Morris says he has received no BHR payouts, and Hunter's attorney Chris Clark said in 2021 that Hunter held no interest 'directly or indirectly' in BHR or Skaneateles. The sources opened give no purchase price for either the original stake or the transfer.
conflicting_figures: Washington Examiner (July 2020) reported that Chinese business records still showed Hunter's 10% stake despite his promise to leave the board.
validation_path: Chinese corporate registry records for Bohai Harvest RST (Shanghai) Equity Investment Fund Management Co., which are public through Chinese registry services. Morris's transcribed-interview transcript (Jan. 18, 2024) was released by House Oversight.

title: Hunter Biden’s art sells during the term: Kevin Morris buys $875,000 of it, Elizabeth Hirsh Naftali $94,000
description: Gallerist Georges Bergès told House investigators that Hunter Biden's lender Kevin Morris bought $875,000 of Hunter's art through a business entity in January 2023, and that Democratic donor Elizabeth Hirsh Naftali bought pieces for $42,000 (Feb. 2021) and $52,000 (Dec. 2022). In 2021 the White House had described an arrangement under which 'He will not know, we will not know who purchases his art,' but Bergès testified Hunter knew both buyers and that he never spoke with the White House about the art.
people: Hunter Biden (Artist and seller); Kevin Morris (Largest buyer ($875,000)); Elizabeth Hirsh Naftali (Buyer ($94,000 total); later appointed to a federal commission (BF-16)); Georges Bergès (Gallerist; testified to House committees (Jan. 2024))
investigation_status: Examined in House Oversight's Jan. 2024 transcribed interview with Bergès. No charges.
dispute: House Republicans said Bergès's testimony showed the confidentiality arrangement did not work: Hunter knew the buyers, who accounted for about 70% of his sales by value (Artnet). Comer's readout says Morris bought about half of the roughly $1.5 million Hunter sold, which reduced what Hunter owed him. Per the Democratic memo (Aug. 2024), Bergès testified Joe Biden had no role in pricing the art and that he had no reason to think Joe Biden benefited. Bergès said no buyer discussed political favors (NBC). Psaki later clarified the White House did not craft the arrangement (NBC).
conflicting_figures: Total sold: about $1.5 million (Comer readout); the totals were not stated by NBC, Artnet or Hyperallergic. DOE said she 'timely divested of all conflicting assets that were known at the time of her confirmation' and that agency ethics officials had deemed the six holdings non-conflicting. OGE certified the transaction report on June 26, 2023.

title: Hunter Biden plea agreement announced: two tax misdemeanors plus gun-charge diversion
description: U.S. Attorney David Weiss's office filed an agreement under which Hunter Biden would plead guilty to two misdemeanor counts of willfully failing to pay federal income tax for 2017 and 2018, years with taxable income 'in excess of $1.5 million' each and 'more than $100,000' owed each year. A pretrial diversion agreement would cover a felony charge of possessing a gun while a drug user. Weiss's office said 'The investigation is ongoing.'
people: Hunter Biden (Defendant); David Weiss (U.S. Attorney for Delaware (Trump appointee kept on by the Biden administration, per the Raskin release))
investigation_status: Deal collapsed July 26, 2023 (BF-24).

conflicting_figures: The statement of facts describes failure to pay 'nearly $2 million in taxes on time' (CNN, BF-24), against 'more than $100,000' owed in each of the two charged years (CNBC).

title: IRS whistleblowers Shapley and Ziegler allege DOJ slow-walked and limited the Hunter Biden tax case
description: IRS supervisory agent Gary Shapley and case agent Joseph Ziegler alleged the tax case was mismanaged. Their account: Weiss said at an October 2022 meeting that he was 'not the deciding person on whether charges are filed'; Weiss was blocked from charging in D.C. and California; the IRS had recommended felony and misdemeanor charges; and the Justice Department cut the IRS out after Shapley objected. The House Ways and Means Committee released Shapley's transcript in June 2023, and both men testified publicly before House Oversight on July 19, 2023.
people: Gary Shapley (IRS-CI supervisory special agent; whistleblower); Joseph Ziegler (IRS case agent; whistleblower); Merrick Garland (Attorney General; denied interference)
investigation_status: Allegations are part of the impeachment record. No DOJ finding of misconduct is documented in the sources opened.
dispute: Garland (June 23, 2023): Weiss 'was given complete authority to make all decisions on his own.' Weiss wrote Rep. Jordan on June 30, 2023 that he had 'ultimate authority' and had 'never been denied the authority to bring charges in any jurisdiction' (NBC). FBI officials Thomas Sobocinski and Ryeshia Holley and IRS official Darrell Waldon did not recall Weiss making the 'not the deciding person' remark, though they agreed Weiss had trouble getting other U.S. attorneys to partner (CNN, Sept. 2023). Weiss and DOJ did not deny that the D.C. and California discussions occurred (NBC).
conflicting_figures: The meeting date is given as October 2022 in the sources opened; the commonly cited Oct. 7, 2022 date was not verified.
market_or_venue: House Committees on Ways and Means and Oversight

Prosecutor Leo Wise said yes, defense attorney Chris Clark disagreed, and Wise replied, 'Then there is no deal.' The judge did not accept the plea, citing concerns about the provision's constitutionality and its placement outside the plea agreement.

investigation_status: Talks hit an 'impasse.' Weiss was made special counsel Aug. 11, 2023 (BF-26).

title: Hijacked SEC X account falsely announces bitcoin ETF approval a day early
description: At 4:11 p.m. ET on Jan. 9, 2024, after a SIM swap gave outsiders control of the SEC's phone number, the @SECGov X account falsely announced approval of spot bitcoin ETFs, sending bitcoin up more than $1,000 and then down more than $2,000 once the SEC called the post unauthorized. The SEC actually approved the ETFs on Jan. 10.
people: Eric Council Jr. (Carried out the SIM swap; paid about $50,000; pleaded guilty); Gary Gensler (SEC Chair impersonated in the false post)
investigation_status: Council, 26, of Athens, Ala., was arrested Oct. 17, 2024, pleaded guilty Feb. 10, 2025 to conspiracy to commit aggravated identity theft, and was sentenced May 16, 2025 to 14 months in prison and three years' supervised release, with $50,000 forfeited. Co-conspirators were not named. The SEC said X Support had disabled multi-factor authentication on the account in July 2023 at staff's request.
conflicting_figures: Council's residence: Athens, Ala. (DOJ) vs Huntsville (SEC OIG). Price move: 'more than $1,000' (DOJ) vs about 2.5% (Wikipedia).
curation_note: Hacked SEC account post; the dollar figure is not a trade size.
announcement: SEC approval of listing and trading of spot bitcoin exchange-traded products
announcer: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Chair Gary Gensler)
validation_path: D.D.C. criminal docket for U.S. v. Council (PACER, public); SEC incident page (public); bitcoin tick data for 4:00-5:30 p.m. ET on Jan. 9, 2024 (exchange APIs, largely free).

It said Kaplan's vague disclosures created an 'appearance' of acting on confidential FOMC information, and that Rosengren's 2020 REIT trades during the Fed's MBS purchases created an appearance of a conflict of interest.

investigation_status: Closed without referral. The OIG found insufficient evidence to refer anyone for law-enforcement review after consulting insider-trading experts. It had issued a closing memo on Powell and Clarida on July 11, 2022.

title: BLS economist emails unpublished CPI details to Wall Street 'super users'
description: A BLS staffer sent restricted or inaccurate CPI information to outside users on Jan. 31 (19 recipients), Feb. 15 (7) and Feb. 27, 2024 (50), the last suggesting that January's owners'-equivalent-rent surge reflected a calculation change, according to the Labor Department inspector general. BLS called the email a mistake, and firms named in the exchanges included JPMorgan, BlackRock, Citadel, Millennium and Brevan Howard (Bloomberg).
people: Erika McEntarfer (BLS Commissioner; recipient of Sen. Cassidy's April 26, 2024 letter); Bill Cassidy (Ranking member, Senate HELP Committee; demanded records and corrective actions)
investigation_status: BLS said the problem appeared isolated to one staffer, who stopped answering user questions. A Labor Department team of experts (formed Sept. 27, 2024; report Nov. 25, 2024) found the incidents isolated and caused by human error. The DOL inspector general (report 17-26-001-11-001, June 26, 2026) wrote that 'no evidence came to our attention that the information the groups received gave them an advantage over other users.'
conflicting_figures: Cassidy's letter says traders acted on the housing information for over an hour before BLS told recipients to disregard it. The DOL OIG found no evidence that recipients gained an advantage. The team of experts mentions only the 50-recipient email; the OIG lists three dates.
announcement: January 2024 CPI release, whose owners'-equivalent-rent jump prompted the inquiries
market_or_venue: Inflation-sensitive markets (Treasuries, TIPS, fed funds futures)
validation_path: DOL OIG and team-of-experts reports (public); Cassidy letter (public); redacted email records released to Bloomberg; intraday Treasury and TIPS futures on Feb. 27, 2024 (CME, commercial) to test the claim that traders acted on it.

title: House E&C releases emails on 2010 Kaiser White House contacts about Solyndra

In an Oct. 22, 2010 email about a Las Vegas dinner with Obama, Kaiser wrote that he 'never mentioned Solyndra directly'.
people: George Kaiser (Solyndra investor via Argonaut / family foundation; subject of emails); Cliff Stearns (Republican chair of the investigating subcommittee; said Kaiser had 'ready access' to the West Wing); Henry Waxman; Diana DeGette (Democratic committee leaders; issued 8-page rebuttal memo)
investigation_status: Part of the House E&C investigation that produced the Aug. 2, 2012 majority report (OF-12); the White House said it had produced 85,000 pages under subpoena.

Kaiser's spokesman said Kaiser 'had no discussions with the government regarding the loan to Solyndra' and Kaiser told staff 'I have never lobbied for Solyndra'; one email shows Kaiser discouraging subordinates from lobbying the White House because DOE/Chu might 'resent the intervention' (AP). Energy Secretary Chu testified on Nov. 17, 2011: 'I did not make any decision based on political considerations' (AP).

The Post said the records do not establish that anyone pressured DOE to benefit political contributors.

validation_path: Emails and memos released by House E&C (2011-2012) and the Post's document set; DOE Loan Programs Office records; public in part.

On May 15, 2013 he told House Judiciary that 'there's no bank, there's no institution, there's no individual that cannot be prosecuted', calling his earlier remarks misconstrued.
people: Eric Holder (testifying Attorney General)

title: Height Securities alert and insurer-stock surge before CMS rate reversal
description: At about 3:40 p.m. ET on April 1, 2013, a Height Securities analyst sent nearly 200 clients a 'flash report' saying 'a deal has been hatched to protect Medicare Advantage rates,' roughly 30 minutes after a Greenberg Traurig lobbyist emailed him at 3:11 p.m.; insurer shares and volume jumped within minutes. After the close (about 4:15 p.m.), CMS announced 2014 rates that turned a projected 2.3% payment decline into a 3.5% increase.
people: Brian Sutter (House Ways and Means health-subcommittee staffer; the SEC said he may have been a source of the lobbyist's information and that he spoke with the lobbyist around 3:00 p.m.; he told FBI and HHS investigators he did not recall discussing the announcement with the firm; never charged); Mark Hayes (Greenberg Traurig lobbyist for Humana who emailed Height (named by Reuters); former Grassley health aide (WSJ via Becker's); said his prediction came from 'very credible sources'; not charged); Marilyn Tavenner (Acting CMS Administrator and nominee whose confirmation the Height note and later-reported communications tied to the alleged deal; no allegation in the sources reviewed that she disclosed information); Kathleen Sebelius (HHS Secretary; directed CMS actuaries to assume physician fees would be held level, which drove the reversal)
investigation_status: SEC opened a probe on Apr. 9, 2013. The FBI, the HHS OIG and, briefly, federal prosecutors also examined it, alongside a Grassley inquiry. SEC subpoena litigation followed (OM-20) and was dropped in Jan. 2017 (OM-23). No one was charged.
dispute: Denials: Humana said it had no advance knowledge and cut ties with Greenberg Traurig; Greenberg Traurig said it did nothing wrong and stopped representing political-intelligence clients; Height said its alert rested on 'solid, sound research.' The tip chain the SEC described ran through congressional staff, not the White House; the SEC also said Sutter contacted at least two CMS employees the week before.
conflicting_figures: Alert time: 3:40 p.m. (S.D.N.Y. opinion) vs. 3:42 p.m. (Grassley, citing WSJ). CMS release: about 4:15 p.m. (opinion) vs. about 4:20 ('20 minutes after the close,' AP) vs. about 4:30 p.m. (Grassley letter); lead time therefore 35-48 minutes. Recipients: 'nearly 200' (opinion) vs. 'more than 150' (Becker's 2014) vs. 'dozens' (AP). Dollar volume: $662.8M 'in the final minutes' (Grassley letter) vs. over $500M in the 18 minutes after 3:42 (Grassley floor speech). MNC's annual report shows the Trump Organization received about $3.7 million in licensing and consulting payments from its Lido and Bali deals with MNC, and it was to earn management fees. On May 13, 2018 Trump tweeted that he and Xi were working to give ZTE 'a way to get back into business, fast.'

title: OGE warns Ross that late divestitures created 'potential for a serious criminal violation'

Ross kept Invesco stock worth $10 million-$50 million past his deadline, during which it gained at least $1.2 million and as much as $6 million; Sun Bancorp, Greenbrier and Air Lease stakes were also divested late. Ross said the same day he had made 'inadvertent errors' and would sell all his equity holdings and buy Treasuries.

investigation_status: OGE found 'no information to contradict' Ross's claim that the lapses were inadvertent; Commerce ethics officials who reviewed his calendar and correspondence found no sign of a criminal violation. Sen. Wyden asked DOJ to investigate on July 13, 2018; no DOJ action was found.

title: Brookfield takes a 99-year lease on Kushner’s 666 Fifth Avenue for about $1.1–1.2B up front; Qatar’s state investment fund is a major Brookfield investor
description: On Aug. 3, 2018 Brookfield announced it had acquired a 100% leasehold interest in the office condominium at 666 Fifth Avenue, Kushner Companies' troubled tower, which had a $1.2B mortgage due in February 2019 (Bloomberg). Brookfield paid about $1.1 billion up front for a 99-year ground lease (Bisnow), or $1.2 billion per Sen. Ron Wyden, letting Kushner Companies pay off its debt. The Qatar Investment Authority held about 9% of Brookfield Property Partners, the lessor's parent, and Wyden says it had invested $1.8B and was BPY's second-largest investor.
people: Jared Kushner (senior White House adviser with family interest in Kushner Companies); Charles Kushner (led the search for partners for 666 Fifth; met Qatari minister Ali Sharif Al Emadi on April 24, 2017 per Wyden); Ron Wyden (Senate Finance chair who investigated the deal)
investigation_status: House Oversight Democrats signaled a probe in 2019 (Axios); Senate Finance Chair Wyden demanded records from Brookfield on Oct. 13, 2022 and said Brookfield twice declined. No charges or findings of wrongdoing.
dispute: Brookfield had said before the deal that 'no Qatar-linked entity has any involvement in, investment in or even knowledge of this potential transaction' (quoted by Wyden, who says it proved false). A QIA spokesman said 'QIA had absolutely no involvement in the 666 Fifth Ave. development' (Bisnow).
conflicting_figures: Up-front lease payment: ~$1.1B (Bisnow) vs $1.2B (Wyden). Debt: $1.2B mortgage due Feb. 2019 (Bloomberg) vs. $1.8B in purchase leverage (Bisnow, 2007). QIA's stake: ~9% (Bisnow); $1.8B invested, second-largest BPY investor (Wyden).
curation_note: Brookfield's up-front payment for the 99-year lease on Kushner Companies' 666 Fifth Avenue, at the low end reported ($1.1B).
validation_path: Brookfield press release and SEC Form 6-K (Aug. 2018); NYC ACRIS lease memoranda for 666 Fifth Ave.; Brookfield Property Partners annual reports (QIA holdings); Senate Finance Committee letter to Bruce Flatt (Oct. 13, 2022).

title: About 420,000 E-mini S&P futures bought late on June 28, 2019, before Trump's G20 'back on track' remarks
description: Vanity Fair (William D. Cohan, Oct. 2019) reported that in the last 30 minutes of trading on Friday, June 28, 2019, buyers took about 420,000 September E-mini S&P 500 contracts, roughly 40% of that day's volume in the contract. On Saturday in Osaka, after the Chicago market had closed, Trump said following his meeting with Xi Jinping that U.S.-China trade talks were 'back on track.' Vanity Fair estimated that the index's roughly 84-point rise implied gains of nearly $1.8 billion ($4,200 per contract). No trader was identified.

dispute: CME Group (Oct. 18, 2019) called the article's claims 'patently false' and said 'these transactions were entered into by a significant number of diverse market participants.' Cohan himself said other factors could explain the trades and that he does not know whether any wrongdoing occurred (Bloomberg, Oct. 21, 2019).
conflicting_figures: Vanity Fair says 'nearly $1.8 billion' for this trade alone; the Yahoo-syndicated summary describes $1.8bn as the profit tied to the largest (June 28) trade. The profit is a hypothetical figure assuming the positions were held through the rally.
curation_note: Vanity Fair's estimate of possible gains if one buyer held the contracts; no trader identified and CME disputes the account. Shown, not added.

title: Trump economic advisers' private Hoover briefings on virus risk circulate to hedge funds in a memo
description: The New York Times reported (Oct. 14, 2020) that while Trump and Larry Kudlow were publicly saying the virus was under control, administration officials including Kudlow and senior economic adviser Tomas Philipson privately discussed it as a concern at a late-February Hoover Institution board meeting in Washington (Stanford Daily; Institutional Investor). Hoover overseer and hedge-fund strategist William Callanan wrote that nearly every official raised the virus 'unprovoked' and emailed his summary to David Tepper of Appaloosa Management; it reached four investment firms within a day, and one investor decided to 'short everything.' Stocks fell through the Feb. 26 close as virus fears were already growing.
people: Tomas Philipson (Briefed Hoover overseers; said he could not estimate the virus's growth impact); Larry Kudlow (Briefed board members the day after Philipson ('contained in the U.S., to date, but now we just don't know')); William Callanan (Wrote and sent the memo); David Tepper (Received the memo; Appaloosa staff circulated it to outside investors)
investigation_status: No SEC, DOJ or congressional investigation found in opened sources.
dispute: Callanan told the NYT his views came from research and public information. Hoover said the meeting was attended only by Hoover affiliates and it knew nothing of the email. A source close to Tepper said the exchange focused on the health crisis, not the administration's views.
conflicting_figures: Meeting length: 'two-day weekend event' (Stanford Daily) vs. 'three days' (Institutional Investor). Range here uses Feb. 24 (Trump's tweet on the first morning) to Feb. 26 (memo-driven trading).
validation_path: NYT article of Oct. 14, 2020 (Kate Kelly and Mark Mazzetti); Hoover Institution board-of-overseers meeting agenda (Feb. 2020); Philipson/Kudlow calendars via FOIA.

curation_note: Academic estimate across all Polymarket since 2024; outside this window and aggregate.
validation_path: Fully replicable from public Polymarket on-chain data (Polygon) and APIs (free). The screen is buy-side only, excludes positions under $500 and cannot catch deliberately small bettors.

title: Special Forces sergeant's alleged Polymarket bets on Maduro's ouster ('Burdensome-Mix')
description: According to the DOJ indictment and CFTC complaint (allegations, not proven), Master Sgt. Gannon Ken Van Dyke helped plan Operation Absolute Resolve. He allegedly opened a Polymarket account around Dec 26 2025 and placed about 13 'Yes' bets totaling about $33,034 on US forces entering Venezuela and Maduro being out by Jan 31 2026, before the Jan 3 2026 capture. Alleged profit is about $409,881.
people: Gannon Ken Van Dyke (Charged defendant (alleged bettor); pleaded not guilty)
investigation_status: Indicted in S.D.N.Y. (No. 26-cr-156); parallel CFTC civil complaint (No. 26-cv-3369); not-guilty plea Apr 28 2026
dispute: NPR calls it the first US criminal case over prediction-market wagers.
conflicting_figures: Amount wagered: $33,034 (DOJ); about $32,000 (NPR, NYT via Boston Globe); nearly $34,000 (Courthouse News, CBS); $38,500 (Mitts & Ofir). Profit: $409,881 (DOJ); more than $404,000 (CFTC); about $485,000 (Mitts & Ofir). Bet window: Dec 27 2025 to the evening of Jan 2 2026 (ABC court coverage, citing prosecutors; my extraction of the DOJ release read 'Jan. 26', likely an extraction or typographical error) vs Dec 30 2025 to Jan 2 2026 (CFTC: more than 436,000 Yes shares in the 'Maduro Out' market). DOJ puts the alleged insider-knowledge window at about Dec 8 2025 through at least Jan 6 2026.
announcement: US forces capture Nicolas Maduro in Caracas (predawn) and the operation is made public
market_or_venue: Polymarket (international platform, Polygon); contracts include 'Maduro Out by January 31, 2026?'
validation_path: Polymarket handle 'Burdensome-Mix': its proxy-wallet trade history stays on-chain even though the account was deleted, readable via Polymarket's Data API, Dune and Polygonscan (free). Court records: PACER, S.D.N.Y. 26-cr-156 and 26-cv-3369 (paid per page; free on CourtListener/RECAP if mirrored). DOJ and CFTC releases are free. KYC, email and brokerage records are in evidence (restricted).
primary_source_title: U.S. Department of Justice (Press Release 26-397) — U.S. soldier charged with using classified information to profit from prediction market bets

Some also hold places on preapproved shortlists for up to nearly $200B, and SpaceX and Anduril account for roughly 97% of the direct cash.
people: Donald Trump Jr. (Investor via 1789 Capital); Eric Trump (Investor via American Ventures (Dominari Holdings))
dispute: White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly: 'no conflicts of interest.' Companies and the White House say all contracts went through standard procurement.
conflicting_figures: User brief: '11 of 15 defense/AI firms with Pentagon business.' Gadget Review's summary says 1789 backed 11 of the 15 companies and gives no count of firms with Pentagon business; I could not open the Post itself. Per the summaries, five firms won their first-ever federal contracts after the brothers invested and Trump took office, and long-term federal commitments excluding SpaceX and Anduril are about $1.8B.
curation_note: Tally or letter citing an aggregate across many awards; annotation only, not added.
validation_path: Rebuild from USAspending (contracts, grants, loans) and SAM.gov by UEI for SpaceX, Anduril, Hadrian, Unusual Machines (mostly subawards), Firehawk, PsiQuantum, Cerebras and Vulcan. Compare award dates with investment dates (Form D, company releases). Shortlist (IDIQ/MAC) ceilings appear in DoD contract announcements.
primary_source_title: Ground News — Washington Post finds Trump sons' funds back defense-tech firms with Pentagon contracts (aggregator summary)

title: Warren, Garcia, Blumenthal and Duckworth ask the DoD IG to investigate awards to Trump-son-linked firms
description: In a letter to DoD Inspector General Platte Moring III, dated Aug 4, 2026 and released Aug 5, the lawmakers cited the Post's $3.2B tally plus $3.1B in options. They asked the IG to identify awards involving companies tied to the Trump family or other officials, check whether ethics rules were followed, and assess proposed FY2027 NDAA ethics rules for OSC. The letter names Anduril (~$1B), SpaceX (~$2.1B), Hadrian, Vulcan, Unusual Machines, PsiQuantum, Cerebras, Firehawk, Aeon and Foundation Future Industries.
people: Donald Trump Jr. (Investor via 1789 Capital); Eric Trump (Investor via American Ventures)
dispute: Denials, per the Post via the Inquirer: Pentagon acting press secretary Joel Valdez said 'No company receives preferential treatment.' White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly called the reporting 'the same, tired narrative.' Trump Jr.'s spokesman Andy Surabian said he does not interface with the federal government for any company he invests in or advises. Trump Organization spokesperson Kimberly Benza called the brothers passive, minority investors with no role in awarding contracts. 1789 declined to comment.
conflicting_figures: User brief attributes the Aug 5 IG request to 'Warren/Kim/Blumenthal'; the signers were Warren, Garcia, Blumenthal and Duckworth (Kim co-signed the Jan 22 letter). The letter dates the Vulcan loan to Aug 2025, but OSC's commitment came in Nov 2025 (1789 invested in Aug 2025). Anduril receipts since 1789's investment: ~$1B here vs ~$1.8B across 135 contracts in ABC's Oct 7 original.
curation_note: Tally or letter citing an aggregate across many awards; annotation only, not added.
validation_path: The letter PDF is public. Check the DoD IG ongoing-work list for any announced evaluation (public if opened). Award data as in D-11.
primary_source_title: Office of Sen. Elizabeth Warren — Warren, Garcia, Blumenthal, Duckworth urge DoD watchdog to investigate $3.2 billion in government awards to companies tied to Trump sons

title: ACDC report: 152 'Orca' wallets won about $8M on US military markets (97.2% win rate)
description: The Anti-Corruption Data Collective's report 'Classifying Insider Trading Risk' found 152 wallets that bet mainly or only on US military-event markets. They placed about $2M in trades and won about $8M (an average of $52,514 per wallet) with a 97.2% win rate on longshot bets. Their bets preceded similar bets by 648 whale and bot wallets.
investigation_status: ACDC says only subpoena power can identify the insiders
conflicting_figures: $8M is reported as 'won' (Casino.org) and 'profited' (CNN). It is unclear whether it is net of the roughly $2M staked. ACDC's June 2026 piece (A-22) gave a lower figure: 'more than half' of military longshots succeed.
curation_note: Aggregate across 152 wallets; not added.
validation_path: Replicable from public Polymarket data (free) using the ACDC rule: stake over $2,500 at a price under $0.35. The ACDC report PDF is public.

title: Powerus closes merger with Trump-backed Aureus Greenway and lists on Nasdaq as PUSA

Reuters reported that the brothers' fund, American Ventures, would hold about 9.9%.

title: ABC News analysis of more than $6B in deals is deleted, then republished with a correction
description: ABC News reported on Oct 7, 2026 that defense firms backed by Trump Jr. and Eric Trump had more than $6B in active or promised government contracts, including about $1.8B across 135 contracts to Anduril since 1789 Capital's June 2025 investment (SAM.gov data). ABC pulled the story within a day and on Oct 9 republished an unbylined version under a new headline, with an editor's note acknowledging errors about investments, contracts and chronology.
people: Donald Trump Jr. (1789 Capital partner; per a 1789 spokesperson, not on its three-person investment committee); Eric Trump (Investor in companies named in the analysis)
dispute: A Pentagon official said political connections play no role. The brothers' spokesperson said their investments rest on 'independent business judgment' and called the coverage 'a deliberate distortion of the facts.' Per Semafor, ABC producer Peter Charalambous told Anduril and Powerus the story was 'published prematurely.'
conflicting_figures: The original said 1789 'claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment.' The correction says the $2.5B was Anduril's whole round and 1789 invested $50M; Anduril says 1789 holds about 0.13% with no major investor rights. I could not confirm whether the $6B total and the $1.8B/135-contract figures survived the revision. 1789 spokeswoman Alexa Henning said many of the companies had contracts under both Biden and Trump.
curation_note: Tally or letter citing an aggregate across many awards; annotation only, not added.

title: Bloomberg: Selig adviser told staff to retract the Mar 23 insider-trading referral
description: Bloomberg reported that CFTC market-oversight analysts referred the Mar 23 trades to the Division of Enforcement. It said Mel Gunewardena, adviser to Chair Selig, then told a market-oversight supervisor to retract the referral and wanted to take over gathering the trade data himself. A former enforcement director said such a step would have been 'never done' in prior administrations.
people: Mel Gunewardena (Reportedly told a supervisor to retract the referral (Bloomberg, unnamed sources); did not respond to Bloomberg); Michael Selig (CFTC Chairman whose adviser gave the instruction; opened sources do not say Selig directed or knew of it)
investigation_status: CFTC spokesman Zach Fulton: 'The CFTC does not confirm or deny any investigation.' A source said an extensive investigation begun in late March is ongoing and all referred entities remain under investigation, calling contrary reporting 'false and malicious'. An official said the review was broadened internationally because the original findings were US-focused. DOJ has a parallel probe, per a person familiar.
conflicting_figures: No opened source gives the date of the instruction. The supervisor had left the agency by July 2026 (DCNF), and Gunewardena was hired 'weeks before' the order (TNR). The NPR Illinois summary implies the instruction came on Mar 23, which conflicts with the other accounts and is likely a summary error. The $580M is the FT/Bloomberg notional for the referred trades, not profit.
announcement: Trump strike-delay post (see A-01)
market_or_venue: CFTC (oversight of Brent/WTI trades of Mar 23 2026)
validation_path: FOIA to the CFTC for the Division of Market Oversight referral and its withdrawal, and Gunewardena's communications about it (likely exemptions 5 and 7(A)); CFTC Inspector General complaint or review; Senate Agriculture or Banking oversight letters. Gunewardena's hiring date may appear in CFTC announcements or his OGE Form 278 (public on request).
primary_source_title: The New Republic — Trump official tries to kill report on perfectly timed oil trades
